summary.text: Hematite is an iron-oxide mineral whose name comes from the Greek word for blood, after the red color of some varieties.
Large deposits occur in banded iron formations, and it can also settle in layers in standing water or form through volcanic activity.
Its color is often used as a pigment, and the earliest known human use of the powdery mineral dates to 164,000 years ago.

facts.label: Magnetism
facts.value: Not noticeably attracted to an ordinary magnet

items.prompt: You hold an ordinary fridge magnet next to a lump of hematite. What happens?

options.label: It snaps firmly to the magnet
It pushes the magnet away
Almost nothing noticeable
It becomes a permanent magnet

items.explain: Hematite responds only very feebly to a magnetic field and, unlike magnetite, is not noticeably attracted to an ordinary magnet.

items.prompt: Roughly how long ago did people first use powdered hematite, as far as is known today?

options.label: About 5,000 years ago
About 30,000 years ago
About 1 million years ago
About 164,000 years ago

items.explain: The earliest known use is 164,000 years ago at the Pinnacle Point caves in what is now South Africa.

items.prompt: Red ochre and yellow ochre both get their color from hematite. What makes them differ?

options.label: Yellow ochre's hematite is hydrated
Yellow ochre contains no iron
Red ochre has been heated in a kiln
Red ochre is mixed with copper

items.explain: Red ochre contains unhydrated hematite, while yellow ochre contains hydrated hematite.

items.prompt: How was hematite detected on the planet Mars?

options.label: A rover drilled into the rock
An orbiting spectrometer spotted its signature
Astronauts brought back samples
Telescopes on Earth saw red patches

items.explain: Infrared spectrometers on NASA's Mars Global Surveyor and 2001 Mars Odyssey, orbiting Mars, picked up its spectral signature.

items.prompt: Why might an old iron mine's waste piles be worth reprocessing?

options.label: They slowly turn into pure iron
They hold gold left by the miners
They still contain hematite to recover
They are needed to refill the mine

items.explain: Hematite is present in iron-mine tailings, and a process called magnetation gleans it from old tailings in Minnesota.

items.prompt: Hematite can collect in layers at the bottom of a still lake. How does it get there?

options.label: It drops out of the water and settles
Fish carry it down from the surface
It grows from lake plants
Rivers grind it out of the lakebed

items.explain: The mineral may precipitate in standing water and collect in layers at the bottom.
